commenti.body: I've been a fan for years. Susan Wheeler is a captivating example of the "capable protagonist," who the audience attaches to out of an interest in seeing what clever way she will next escape trouble. I showed the film to my sister a few years back and she noted that the feminist themes had remained quite relevant.
Great point. Bujold’s intensity (and her accent) made her especially compelling.

Didn't know it hit movie theatres back then. Seems to fall into the set of films (don't say genre!) of low-key 1st world dystopias ......Terminal Man, Logan's Run, Looker, Embryo also.

Some of them ...naaah, a lot of them have Michael Critchton's authorship all over them
Very much so. I read the Terminal Man book but have yet to see the movie - it’s hard to find.
tbh you're not missing much. My recollection was it was way too over-earnest. Think : Rollerball (70s incarnation)
